key_insight: The paper turns deep-space relay scheduling into a goal-oriented reinforcement learning problem that prioritizes bundles by mission value, freshness, and fairness rather than simple FIFO order.
engineering_relevance: This is directly useful for deep-space network relays because it provides a control strategy for scarce storage and intermittent contacts while improving delivery utility across heterogeneous planetary sources.
method: Model relay control as a constrained semi-Markov decision process (CSMDP).
Use masked Lagrangian PPO to learn scheduling, dropping, and flow-control policies.
Apply feasibility-aware action masking so only bundles that can finish within the remaining contact window are transmitted.
evidence_signal: DTNSim simulations reported better age-based utility and inter-flow fairness than baseline schedulers such as FIFO.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate contact-window prediction and the ability of the learned policy to generalize across different deep-space traffic patterns and mission priority settings.
paper_title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
